original: A tall compact cluster of hollow upright sea-sponge/coral tubes sits on a broad cobalt faceted rubble base, isolated on transparency.
Five prominent hot-pink tubes form a central tallest tube and staggered left/right tubes; a short violet tube is at the front and another violet tube peeks behind the upper left side.
Tube mouths read as polygonal dark recesses with thin, sharply cut pink or violet rims. Long straight facets and abrupt tonal bands dominate the walls.
Base rocks are low and blocky with large dark blue faces; the exposed front is relatively plain. The original feels rigid and strongly saturated.
target: The target keeps the same recognizable staggered hollow tube coral family, central height hierarchy, pink/violet palette and blue rocky grounding.
Rims are thick, visibly rounded and irregular rather than straight cut; warm peach/cream highlight bands wrap the lips and distinguish mouth thickness.
The dark mouths have readable inner walls and bottom depth; smooth broad wall lighting, soft edge transitions and gentle taper/curvature give the tubes plush sculpted volume.
Subtle darker oval spots and long organic tone shapes decorate the pink walls without displacing the primary silhouettes.
Blue base rocks have larger individually readable rounded masses and brighter cyan upper planes. Small violet hollow sprouts/pebbles and curving green seaweed add grounded secondary life.

The additional accents are concentrated near the base and gaps, while the main tube mouths and central silhouette remain dominant. This is a visible design direction, not proof that every added element fits the native geometry or temporal envelope.
warmSoftReference: The reference plant uses strong green and gold/orange colors, broad facets and a compact readable silhouette.

Its soft cartoon quality comes from warm luminous edge highlights, rounded/beveled transitions, coherent shading and deep but gentle contact shadows. It does not imply that the coral should become muted or uniformly smooth.
possibleNativeWorkAfterFrozenDispatch: Native rounded lip thickness and inner cavities could carry the target mouth readability.
Controlled tube taper/curvature, softer broad-face lighting and restrained material variation could translate the wall treatment.
Purposeful base-rock massing and modest organic accents may improve the construction if the frozen source envelope and looping motion contract permit them.

observedFacts: Actual collection contains one empty ground root and ten meshes: seven hollow-tube meshes and three rubble meshes, parented to the root.

Root transform is location (0,0,0), rotation (0,0,0), scale (1,1,1) at inspection. Raw mesh world bounds at frame 1 are x [-0.5,0.5], y [-0.5,0.5], z [0,1.3350000381469727]. This is an observed original bound, not a self-issued hard constraint.
Each tube has 72 vertices and 62 polygons; each rubble mesh has 32 vertices and 26 polygons. All measured mesh faces are flat shaded, have no modifiers, and have no UV layers.

Seven tube meshes have animation data; three rubble meshes and the root do not. Scene frame range is 1 through 12. Motion has not been altered or fully characterized in this bounded initial inspection.

The tube materials use separate pink/violet outer and dark inner materials; rocks have cobalt/cobaltTop/cobaltDark materials. Material graphs include geometry-driven ramp/mix nodes and Principled shading.

The full original library contains packed dish images unrelated to this collection; none of the inspected coral meshes has an image node in its listed material graphs. Only actual-used asset dependencies will be retained for a candidate.
